decisions.context: The brief describes document classification at millions per day, with seasonal volume swings, multiple consuming teams, and a need to detect quality drift.
decisions.rationale: Throughput and seasonal elasticity lead because the system must handle millions of documents per day; drift visibility and shared access follow as explicit operational needs.

decisions.context: Classification results must be made available to several teams, and the brief does not specify a per-document latency target.

alternatives.label: Data batch based model serving
cons: Availability: results wait for a batch

alternatives.label: Microservice based model serving
pros: Availability: results served in real time

alternatives.label: Hybrid online/offline model serving
pros: Flexibility: supports online and batch results
cons: Cost: two serving paths to operate

decisions.rationale: Throughput decides: batch serving fits the stated high volume and avoids assuming a real-time requirement. The trade-off is that consumers receive results on the batch schedule.
consequences: Consumers read results from shared storage.
Result freshness depends on batch cadence.

decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive daily, but the brief gives no requirement for continuous, per-document processing.

alternatives.label: Data ingestion in batches
pros: Throughput: groups documents for bulk intake
cons: Availability: intake may wait for a batch

decisions.rationale: High throughput decides: batch intake groups work efficiently and the brief does not demand immediate classification. This gives up continuous arrival handling.
consequences: Intake and classification cadence must be coordinated.
Batch sizes can be adjusted for seasonal volume.

decisions.context: The system processes a large, seasonally variable volume, and no strict response-time target is stated.
decisions.rationale: Throughput decides: batch processing matches bulk document intake and seasonal load variation. The cost is delayed results between processing runs.
consequences: Processing capacity can be allocated per run.
A backlog may build between runs.

decisions.context: The volume reaches millions of documents per day and changes significantly over the year, so processing work needs to scale across partitions.

alternatives.label: Data partitioning in data pipeline
pros: Throughput: partitions work for parallel processing

alternatives.label: Data pipeline per data set
cons: Elasticity: scaling tied to dataset pipelines

decisions.rationale: High throughput decides: partitioning allows concurrent processing within a pipeline. We accept the operational work of coordinating partitions.
consequences: Work must be divided and results reconciled.
Capacity can scale with partitioned workload.

decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. The design space distinguishes model performance monitoring from logging data and predictions; a checked design point flagged these as alternatives in one dimension.

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
cons: Throughput: metrics must be aggregated at scale

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
cons: Cost: data volume to retain and inspect

alternatives.label: No in-production monitoring
cons: Drift visibility: quality changes go unseen

decisions.rationale: Detect quality drift decides: directly monitoring model performance serves the stated need. We give up the additional diagnostic detail available from retaining and monitoring inputs and predictions.
consequences: Define performance measures and alert thresholds.
Monitoring does not by itself specify how to correct drift.

decisions.decision: How to adjust models after monitoring
decisions.context: Monitoring can reveal drift, but the brief does not authorize or describe automatic model updates; classification quality is operationally important.

alternatives.label: Automated model adjustment
pros: Recovery time: can trigger adjustments automatically
cons: Quality control: changes occur without manual review

decisions.rationale: Quality control decides: the brief requires drift visibility but gives no policy for safe automatic adaptation. We accept slower recovery so operators can review model changes.
consequences: Operators must review alerts and adjust models.
Retraining and promotion procedures remain to be defined.

uncovered: Per-document latency and service availability targets
LLM provider, model selection, rate limits, and cost controls
Data retention, privacy, security, and access control
Quality metric definitions, labels, and drift thresholds
Batch cadence, retry handling, and failure recovery
Result schema and inter-team access contract
Model and prompt versioning and reproducibility
Human review and escalation for low-confidence predictions
